newsitem.title: USA: Land developer in N. Calif. jail ahead of hearing.
newsitem.headline: Land developer in N. Calif. jail ahead of hearing.

text.p: A former developer linked to several failed land deals in California has been moved to a San Mateo County, Calif., jail pending a hearing on whether he will stand trial on charges of securities violations.

Chuck Finney, deputy district attorney for San Mateo County, said on Thursday that G. Michael Montross was now being held in a San Mateo County jail pending a December preliminary hearing in municipal court, the first major hearing of the criminal case.
The hearing was scheduled for December 9 and December 10, Finney said.
At the preliminary hearing, evidence will be presented to a magistrate to determine whether Montross will be held over for trial in Superior Court.

Montross was taken into custody in June after more than two years on the run. Before he was moved to San Mateo, he served time in Los Angeles for allegedly making false statements on a passport application, Finney said.

More than two years ago, San Mateo County District Attorney's office filed 93 counts of securities violations against Montross related to a number of failed land deals, including a land deal in Nevada County, Calif.
Montross has pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Bonds issued by Nevada County for the land deal are currently the subject of a Securities and Exchange Commission investigation. Finney said the charges brought by his office do not involve the bonds.
A warrant for Montross's arrest was issued in December 1993. But investigators could not find Montross.
Investigators believe Montross traveled around the country with the proceeds of his alleged crimes as a developer, eventually settling in Newport Beach, Calif.
Authorities believe Montross was preparing to leave for Costa Rica when he was caught.
An attorney representing Montross was not immediately available for comment.
